blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless unit heats water as it flows. Open a tap, and water runs through a heat exchanger where a burner or element warms it instantly. There's no tank to keep hot, so no standby loss, and no running out halfway through the third shower. Each unit can heat a set number of gallons per minute, so it's sized to how many fixtures you run at once. With well water, regular descaling keeps the heat exchanger clean.

blocks.h2: Is Tankless Right for Your Algonquin Home?
blocks.intro: Tankless installation and repair are common requests from Algonquin homeowners. Here's what decides the fit.

items.body: Back-to-back showers in the morning are where tankless shines, as long as the unit is sized for it.
Builder gas lines from the 1990s and 2000s are often sized for a furnace and a 40-gallon tank. We check before quoting.
Minerals build in the heat exchanger. A working softener and regular descaling keep it running well.

items.q: Can a tankless heater keep up with a big family?
items.preview: Yes, if it's sized for your peak use.
items.answer: Yes, if it's sized for the number of showers and appliances you run at the same time. Very large homes may need a bigger unit or two.

items.q: How often should a tankless unit be descaled?
items.preview: Regularly, often about once a year with well water.
items.answer: With well water, often about once a year. A softener ahead of the unit can stretch that.

items.q: My tankless unit shows an error code. Can you fix it?
items.preview: Yes. Tell us the code when you call.
items.answer: Yes. Most codes point to ignition, flame, flow or scale issues. Give us the code and we'll come prepared.

items.q: Will I need a bigger gas line?
items.answer: Sometimes. We check the existing line and include any upgrade in the flat price.
